news.headline: Darling Ingredients Inc.
news.quote: $1.2 billion cash deal to buy collagen producer Gelnex

touches.claim: The company carries substantial debt, $3.5 billion at October 3, 2026, with a leverage ratio of 1.7X. The 10-K lists substantial indebtedness as a risk.

The Food Ingredients segment, including collagen, faces substitute competition: plant-based and synthetic hydrocolloids, and artificial casings. The segment improved in 2026, with nine-month segment operating income of 170,541 against 125,724 (table in thousands).

Cash generation and balance-sheet capacity support Darling's competitiveness, but debt is a named risk. Nine-month operating cash flow was 1,147,713 against 619,106 and included 456,277 of distributions from DGD and other unconsolidated subsidiaries. Capex was 343,515 (table in thousands). The covenant leverage ratio was 1.7X and net debt fell by about $420 million in the quarter.

Cash generation is funding deleveraging. Operating cash flow was 1,147,713 against 619,106 over nine months, helped by distributions of earnings from DGD and other unconsolidated subsidiaries of 456,277 against 132,802 (table in thousands). Long-term debt net of current portion fell to 3,414,433 from 3,862,243, and net debt was reduced by approximately $420 million in the quarter.

Capital is going into reinvestment and buybacks. Capital expenditures were 343,515 against 224,045 over nine months, and the company estimates approximately $450.0 million for the year. Repurchases of common stock were 149,326 against 34,668 (table in thousands). This requires continued cash generation.

Portfolio reshaping is a source of change. The company spent 122,238 on acquisitions and received 152,886 from disposal of a business, with a gain on sale of businesses of 63,473 in the quarter (table in thousands). It sold its casings business in the quarter and a substantial portion of its grease trap business. The remaining businesses must make up the earnings of the divested units.

Food Ingredients grew modestly. Quarterly net sales were $415,798 against $380,574, and segment operating income was $44,796 against $41,799 (table in thousands). Further growth depends on the segment's collagen and casings margins, which the annual MD&A says follow finished-goods price moves over a long processing time. The casings business has since been sold.

news.why: A $1.2 billion cash acquisition of collagen producer Gelnex expands the Food Ingredients business while materially impacting cash, debt, and deleveraging capacity.

The 10-K had flagged about $25.6 million of restructuring and impairment charges tied to casings.
quotes: The Company sold its natural casings business (known as CTH) in the third quarter of fiscal 2026.
restructuring and impairment charges primarily related to our natural casings business of approximately $25.6 million

competitive_position.claim: Tariffs are a named uncertainty but have not had a material impact on results to date. Darling and DGD have applied for and made some tariff refund recoveries after the Supreme Court decision on IEEPA tariffs.
quotes: While to date these tariffs have not had a material impact on our results of operations
The Company and its DGD Joint Venture have since applied for and made certain tariff recoveries.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited items; the dependence on DGD is inferred from the cash flow line
competitive_position.claim: Cash generation and balance-sheet capacity support Darling's competitiveness, but debt is a named risk. Nine-month operating cash flow was 1,147,713 against 619,106 and included 456,277 of distributions from DGD and other unconsolidated subsidiaries. Capex was 343,515 (table in thousands). The covenant leverage ratio was 1.7X and net debt fell by about $420 million in the quarter.
quotes: The preliminary leverage ratio as measured by the company’s bank covenant was 1.7X as of Oct. 3, 2026.
Our substantial indebtedness could adversely affect our financial condition

financial_health.basis: stated in the balance sheet and the earnings release
financial_health.claim: Cash on hand is small next to the debt. Cash and cash equivalents were 121,716 (table in thousands) at quarter end, and the company reports $1.7 billion available under its committed revolving credit agreement.
quotes: As of October 3, 2026, Darling Ingredients had $121.7 million in cash and cash equivalents, and $1.7 billion available under its committed revolving credit agreement.

financial_health.claim: Total debt outstanding was $3.5 billion at quarter end. Net debt, defined as total debt less cash and cash equivalents, was 3,366,726 (table in thousands).
quotes: Total debt outstanding as of Oct. 3, 2026, was $3.5 billion.

financial_health.claim: The preliminary covenant leverage ratio was 1.7X. Management expects to end the year with net debt at or below $3.0 billion and a ratio below 1.5X.
quotes: The preliminary leverage ratio as measured by the company’s bank covenant was 1.7X as of Oct. 3, 2026.
the company anticipates ending fiscal year 2026 with net debt at or below $3.0 billion, with a leverage ratio below 1.5X.

financial_health.basis: stated in the balance sheet and cash flow statement
financial_health.claim: Debt has fallen. Long-term debt net of current portion went from 3,862,243 to 3,414,433 (table in thousands) over the nine months. Payments on the revolving credit facility of 1,228,752 exceeded borrowings of 826,698 (table in thousands).
quotes: Payments on revolving credit facility | (1,228,752) | (1,060,053)

financial_health.basis: stated in the cash flow statement and the earnings release
financial_health.claim: Operating cash flow for the nine months was 1,147,713 versus 619,106 a year earlier (table in thousands). Capital expenditures were 343,515, and the company estimates about $450.0 million for the full year.
quotes: Net cash provided by operating activities | 1,147,713 | 619,106
The company estimates capital expenditures to be approximately $450.0 million for fiscal year 2026.

financial_health.basis: stated in the earnings release; the policy dependence is stated in the 10-K risk factors
financial_health.claim: Part of the cash generation comes from Diamond Green Diesel (DGD). In the third quarter the company received $171.0 million in cash from DGD, of which about $137.6 million came from Production Tax Credit sales and about $33.4 million from dividends.
quotes: Received $171.0 million in cash distributions from Diamond Green Diesel (DGD)
The company received approximately $33.4 million in dividends and approximately $137.6 million from Production Tax Credit sales from DGD in the third quarter.

financial_health.basis: stated in the cash flow statement; the interpretation is inferred
financial_health.claim: Reported net income overstates cash earnings. The cash flow statement removes (630,206) of equity income from DGD and other unconsolidated subsidiaries (table in thousands) and adds back only 456,277 of distributions of earnings. Deferred taxes of 132,525 were also added back.
quotes: Distributions of earnings from Diamond Green Diesel and other unconsolidated subsidiaries | 456,277 | 132,802

financial_health.basis: stated in the cash flow statement
financial_health.claim: Working capital absorbed cash in inventories and prepaid expenses, while payables and accruals released it. The changes were (106,969) and 158,560 respectively (table in thousands).
quotes: Inventories and prepaid expenses | (106,969) | (8,553)

financial_health.basis: stated in the cash flow and income statements
financial_health.claim: Asset sales supplied cash outside operations. Proceeds from disposal of a business were 152,886 (table in thousands), reported in investing activities, against a 63,473 gain on sale of businesses that the cash flow statement deducts from operating cash flow.
quotes: Proceeds from disposal of business | 152,886 | 0

financial_health.basis: stated in the cash flow statement
financial_health.claim: Cash also went to DGD and to shareholders. Investment in DGD was 191,898 and repurchases of common stock were 149,326 (table in thousands). A 150,000 loan to DGD was repaid in the same period.
quotes: Repurchase of common stock | (149,326) | (34,668)

financial_health.basis: stated in the balance sheet; the sufficiency judgement is inferred
financial_health.claim: The only debt classified as falling due within a year on the balance sheet is a current portion of long-term debt of 74,009 (table in thousands), down from 75,217. This is small next to the committed revolver availability of $1.7 billion.
quotes: Current portion of long-term debt | 74,009 | 75,217

financial_health.claim: The debt stack includes senior secured credit facilities and notes at 6%, 5.25% and 4.5% that were outstanding at quarter end. The release says management also uses Adjusted EBITDA to measure compliance with the financial covenants under these instruments.
quotes: Senior Secured Credit Facilities, 6% Notes, 5.25% Notes and 4.5% Notes that were outstanding at October 3, 2026

financial_health.basis: stated in the earnings release and income statement
financial_health.claim: Earnings that support debt service are strongly DGD-driven. Third-quarter Combined Adjusted EBITDA was $514.3 million, of which DGD's share was 204,205 (table in thousands). Interest expense for the quarter was 51,460.
quotes: Combined Adjusted EBITDA was $514.3 million, compared to $244.9 million for third quarter 2025

financial_health.claim: Management reaffirms full-year Combined Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $2.2-$2.3 billion. Nine-month Combined Adjusted EBITDA was about $1.7 billion.
quotes: Darling Ingredients reaffirms fiscal year 2026 Combined Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $2.2-$2.3 billion

financial_health.basis: stated in the 10-K risk factor summary
financial_health.claim: The company's own risk factors flag leverage as a risk. The 10-K lists substantial indebtedness and the ability to generate enough cash to service debt among its key risks.
quotes: Our substantial indebtedness could adversely affect our financial condition;

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the income statement and the earnings release; the mechanism is inferred from the release text.
growth_thesis.claim: Diamond Green Diesel (DGD) equity income swung from losses to large profits. It was 165,636 (table in thousands) in the latest quarter against (45,844) a year earlier, and 623,029 against (70,367) over nine months. DGD also paid Darling $171.0 million in cash distributions in the quarter.
quotes: Received $171.0 million in cash distributions from Diamond Green Diesel (DGD)

growth_thesis.basis: The dependence on government programs is stated in the risk factors; the link to the recent per-gallon figures is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: For DGD profit to continue, volumes and per-gallon margins must hold, and government programs must stay supportive. In the quarter DGD sold/shipped 314.9 million gallons with DGD Adjusted EBITDA per gallon of $1.30.
quotes: Our renewable energy businesses, including the DGD Joint Venture, are highly dependent on government programs, incentives and regulatory frameworks, which are subject to change and uncertainty.

growth_thesis.basis: Figures are stated in the release segment table; the mechanism is inferred from the annual MD&A description.
growth_thesis.claim: The Feed Ingredients segment, the core rendering business, grew sales and profit in the quarter. Net sales were $1,206,702 against $1,029,115, and segment operating income was $150,839 against $90,406 (table in thousands). Management called the core business's performance exceptional.
quotes: Our core business delivered another quarter of exceptional performance, demonstrating its resilience and strong cash flow generation

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the risk factors and annual MD&A.
growth_thesis.claim: Feed segment growth requires continued access to raw materials and steady finished-product prices. Management says procurement is the most competitive aspect of the business, and that raw material volume affects reported gross margin because fixed operating costs are substantial.
quotes: Our management believes that the most competitive aspect of our business is the procurement of raw materials rather than the sale of finished products.
the volume of raw material acquired, which has a direct impact on the amount of finished goods produced, can also have a material effect on the gross margin reported

growth_thesis.basis: Figures are stated in the income statement; the dependence is stated in the 10-K, and the link to growth is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Sales to DGD, a related party and the primary customer for used cooking oil, grew. They were 432,001 against 342,120 in the quarter, and 1,094,147 against 851,602 over nine months (table in thousands). Continued growth requires DGD to keep operating and buying feedstock from Darling.
quotes: The Company’s primary customer for this product is the DGD Joint Venture.

growth_thesis.basis: Figures are stated in the cash flow statement, balance sheet and release; the causal link is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Cash generation is funding deleveraging. Operating cash flow was 1,147,713 against 619,106 over nine months, helped by distributions of earnings from DGD and other unconsolidated subsidiaries of 456,277 against 132,802 (table in thousands). Long-term debt net of current portion fell to 3,414,433 from 3,862,243, and net debt was reduced by approximately $420 million in the quarter.
quotes: Reduced net debt by approximately $420 million

growth_thesis.claim: Management reaffirmed its fiscal 2026 Combined Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $2.2-$2.3 billion. Nine-month Combined Adjusted EBITDA was $1,662,848 (table in thousands). Meeting the guidance depends on DGD and the core segments continuing to perform in the final quarter.
quotes: Darling Ingredients reaffirms fiscal year 2026 Combined Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $2.2-$2.3 billion

growth_thesis.basis: Figures are stated in the cash flow statement and release; the sustainability condition is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Capital is going into reinvestment and buybacks. Capital expenditures were 343,515 against 224,045 over nine months, and the company estimates approximately $450.0 million for the year. Repurchases of common stock were 149,326 against 34,668 (table in thousands). This requires continued cash generation.
quotes: The company estimates capital expenditures to be approximately $450.0 million for fiscal year 2026.

growth_thesis.basis: Figures are stated in the statements; the implication for future earnings is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Portfolio reshaping is a source of change. The company spent 122,238 on acquisitions and received 152,886 from disposal of a business, with a gain on sale of businesses of 63,473 in the quarter (table in thousands). It sold its casings business in the quarter and a substantial portion of its grease trap business. The remaining businesses must make up the earnings of the divested units.
quotes: The Company sold its natural casings business (known as CTH) in the third quarter of fiscal 2026.

growth_thesis.basis: Figures are stated in the release; the conditions are inferred from the annual MD&A.
growth_thesis.claim: Food Ingredients grew modestly. Quarterly net sales were $415,798 against $380,574, and segment operating income was $44,796 against $41,799 (table in thousands). Further growth depends on the segment's collagen and casings margins, which the annual MD&A says follow finished-goods price moves over a long processing time. The casings business has since been sold.
quotes: The Company sold its natural casings business (known as CTH) in the third quarter of fiscal 2026.

material_events.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A overview (P4). The segment placement of CTH is stated in the 10-K business section (P1).
material_events.claim: The company sold its natural casings business (CTH) in the third quarter. The 10-K describes CTH as part of the Food Ingredients segment.
quotes: The Company sold its natural casings business (known as CTH) in the third quarter of fiscal 2026.

material_events.claim: The company sold a substantial portion of its grease trap collection and disposal business in the third quarter, and sold the remaining portion on October 30, 2026.
quotes: The Company sold a substantial portion of its grease trap collection and disposal business in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, and sold the remaining portion of its grease trap collection and disposal business on October 30, 2026.

risks.basis: Figures are stated in the 10-Q and release. The vulnerability to DGD swings is inferred from the year-over-year change and the 10-K discussion of the fuel segment.
risks.claim: Reported profit depends heavily on Diamond Green Diesel (DGD). Nine-month equity in DGD net income was 623,029 (table in thousands), against a loss of (70,367) a year earlier, and DGD was a loss in fiscal 2025 at (48,770) (table in thousands).
quotes: the renewable fuel industry experienced a significant change in the regulatory environment

risks.basis: Stated in the risk-factor and MD&A text. The earnings impact is inferred.
risks.claim: DGD and the renewable fuel businesses depend on government programs, mandates and tax credits that can change. The 10-K describes these programs as subject to change and uncertainty, and the 10-Q repeats that changes could hurt results.
quotes: Our renewable energy businesses, including the DGD Joint Venture, are highly dependent on government programs, incentives and regulatory frameworks, which are subject to change and uncertainty.

risks.basis: Guidance and nine-month result are stated in the release. The risk of a miss is inferred.
risks.claim: The company reaffirmed fiscal 2026 Combined Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $2.2-$2.3 billion, with about $1.7 billion earned in the first nine months. The remaining quarter is unreported, and the company says it cannot predict its commodity-driven results precisely.
quotes: reaffirms fiscal year 2026 Combined Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $2.2-$2.3 billion

risks.basis: Sales figures and the customer statement are stated. The concentration risk is inferred.
risks.claim: DGD is a large related-party customer. Q3 2026 sales to DGD were 432,001 (table in thousands) of total net sales of 1,791,116 (table in thousands), and the 10-K names DGD as the primary customer for used cooking oil.
quotes: The Company’s primary customer for this product is the DGD Joint Venture.

risks.basis: Debt and leverage figures are stated. The risk is mostly inferred and the evidence argues against near-term stress.
risks.claim: The company carries substantial debt, $3.5 billion at October 3, 2026, with a leverage ratio of 1.7X. The 10-K lists substantial indebtedness as a risk.
quotes: Our substantial indebtedness could adversely affect our financial condition

risks.basis: The gain and divestitures are stated. The effect on future earnings is inferred and cannot be sized from the packet.
risks.claim: Q3 net income included a one-off gain on sale of businesses of 63,473 (table in thousands), and the company sold its natural casings and grease trap businesses. Reported earnings are therefore partly non-recurring, and the company is smaller after the sales.
quotes: The Company sold its natural casings business (known as CTH) in the third quarter of fiscal 2026.

unresolved_questions.claim: How much of the swing in DGD equity income to 623,029 (table in thousands) for the nine months, from a loss of (70,367), depends on production tax credit sales such as the $137.6 million received in the third quarter, and would it persist if incentives or margins change?
quotes: The company received approximately $33.4 million in dividends and approximately $137.6 million from Production Tax Credit sales from DGD in the third quarter.
leading to a reduction in incentives and a decrease in margins

unresolved_questions.basis: Stated in P6 that guidance was reaffirmed and that no forward reconciliation is provided; the implied fourth-quarter level is not computed here.
unresolved_questions.claim: What fourth-quarter assumptions (DGD margins, credit sales, core segment results) does the reaffirmed Combined Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $2.2-$2.3 billion rely on, given about $1.7 billion reported for nine months?
quotes: Darling Ingredients reaffirms fiscal year 2026 Combined Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $2.2-$2.3 billion

unresolved_questions.basis: Inferred from the cash flow statement and balance sheet; the purpose of the DGD investment outflow is not stated in the cited items.
unresolved_questions.claim: Will cash distributions from DGD, 456,277 (table in thousands) for the nine months, continue to exceed Darling's own capital funding of DGD, 191,898 (table in thousands), while the equity-method investment balance is rising?

quotes: The Company sold its natural casings business (known as CTH) in the third quarter of fiscal 2026.

quotes: the company anticipates ending fiscal year 2026 with net debt at or below $3.0 billion, with a leverage ratio below 1.5X

under_review.headline: Darling Ingredients Inc.
under_review.why: A $1.2 billion cash acquisition of collagen producer Gelnex expands the Food Ingredients business while materially impacting cash, debt, and deleveraging capacity.

verdict_reason: expected return +11.1 points a year against the required return over 3 years
